title: The Spy in the Shanghai Office
synopsis: Shanghai, 1920: Korea's government in exile works in a small office.
At night, someone sits at the desk with the secret list.
Kim Gu, the police chief, needs proof.
goal: Find out who copied the secret list, prove it to Kim Gu, and stop the copy.

notes: A time worked out from Haesu's note: the light went on at eleven; half of a four-hour candle burned, two hours; the light went out at one in the night, 01:00.
Haesu, the candle and the light are made up.

learning.objective: at eleven, burns for four hours, half of it was gone을 읽고 불이 꺼진 시각(01:00)을 계산한다.
expressions: A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.

play.title: Half a Candle
story: Early morning in a narrow Shanghai lane.
A young clerk hurries past you and drops a folded note.
It is in Hangeul, Korea's own letters. It has no name.
play.letter:
Detective, someone used the list desk last night.
At eleven, the guard saw the light go on.
I left a new candle there. A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.
— a friend in this office
play.question: What time did the light go out? Use four numbers. (Seven in the morning is 07:00.)
hints: The light went on at eleven. How many hours did half the candle burn?
Half of four hours is two hours. Eleven, twelve, one.
play.successMessage: The light went out at one in the night!
transition: Someone sat at the list desk from eleven until one.
The young clerk comes back. "I am Haesu. I wrote that note."
"A spy may be in this office. So I did not sign my note."

feedback.1300: It was night, not the afternoon. One in the night is 01:00.
feedback.2300: Eleven is when the light went ON. When did it go out?
feedback.0300: Only half of the candle burned, not all of it.
feedback.1100: Eleven is when the light went ON. When did it go out?
feedback.0200: Half of four hours is two. Count two hours from eleven.

play.orderFeedback: The right numbers, in the wrong order. Hours first, then minutes.

play.title: The Police Report
story: Kim Gu's police searched it at dawn.
play.letter:
The key is next to the stove. It opens the list desk.
The ink bottle is on the window sill. It is normal office ink.
The thin paper is under the list desk. Names are pressed into it.
— Kim Gu's police
play.question: Which thing shows that the list was copied?
hints: Read each line of the report. Each one says where a thing is.
Copying presses names through the paper. Which thing has names pressed into it?
play.successMessage: The thin paper has names pressed into it. The list was copied!
transition: Someone wrote a copy on top of this thin paper.
His pen pressed the names into it. There is no ink on it.
Haesu frowns. "At night, only clerks have a key to this office."

play.title: The Sign-Out Book
story: By the door hangs the clerks' sign-out book.
Every clerk writes the time they go home.
play.letter:
Mr. Seo: left at half past eleven.
Mr. Nam Giho: left at a quarter past one.
Haesu: left at nine.
Mr. Pak: left at ten.
The night guard: at the front door all night. He has no office key.
play.question: Who was still in the office when the light went out? Type his name.
hints: Your first clue says when the light went out.
A quarter past one is after one. Who left then?
play.successMessage: Only Mr. Nam Giho was still here at one!
transition: Mr. Nam Giho came to the office only last month.
His desk is empty this morning.
Haesu runs to tell Kim Gu.

feedback.SEO: Mr. Seo left at half past eleven. The light burned until one.
feedback.PAK: Mr. Pak left at ten, before the light went on.

lines.text: Three other clerks work here, and me.
At night this office is locked. Only clerks have a key.
Then the copier is a clerk who stayed late.

discovery.title: THE NEW CLERK
discovery.detail: Mr. Nam Giho stayed until a quarter past one. Now tell the police chief.

notes: Mr. Nam's three claims, each refuted by one mission's evidence picked from three cards: nobody at the desk (Haesu's note: the light from eleven to one), nothing copied (the police report: names pressed into thin paper), home at nine (the sign-out book: a quarter past one). Then his coat is searched and the copy found: the answer 'copy_found'.
Kim Gu is real; every word he says is made up (dossier fiction), resting on h1-h3. The spy, the list and the clerks are made up.

clueInputs.note: The light burned from eleven until one.

play.title: The Police Chief
story: At dawn, Kim Gu's police stop Mr. Nam Giho by the river.
Kim Gu comes back up the stairs.
"Mr. Nam says he did nothing," he says. "Show me your proof."
play.letter:
Nobody was at the list desk last night.
Nothing was copied.
I went home at nine.
play.question: Show Kim Gu that each thing Mr. Nam says is wrong.
hints: Each thing Mr. Nam says has one card that shows it is wrong.
Desk: Haesu's Note. Copy: the police report. Nine: the sign-out book.
transition: Sewn inside Mr. Nam's coat is the copied list. It never left Shanghai.
Kim Gu locks the real list and the copy in an iron box.
"Haesu," he says, "you saw the first clue. Thank you."
play.orderFeedback: Show one card for each thing Mr. Nam says.

evidence.name: Kim Gu's Case Note
evidence.description: The copied list was found sewn in Mr. Nam's coat. It never left Shanghai. Haesu's note, the thin paper and the sign-out book proved it.

objectives: Find when the light went out.

intro: Autumn, 1920. You are in Shanghai, a big city in China, as a guest of Kim Gu.
In 1910, Japan took over Korea. Koreans could not rule their own country.
On 1 March 1919, people all over Korea called for independence. This is the March First Movement.
In April 1919, Koreans began their own government here. It works outside Korea, because Japan rules Korea.
It is the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea.
Kim Gu is its police chief. He keeps it safe from spies.
This morning, he is worried. "Someone was at our secret list," he says.
play.caseSummary: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one. Thin paper showed the list was copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, left last. The copy was found in his coat. Haesu, a young clerk, saw the first clue. The Provisional Government began in Shanghai in April 1919, and Kim Gu was its police chief. His police guarded it and watched for spies. Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became its chairman.

notes: PART 10 Case 09; PART 1A (2026-11-09): an independent case. Haesu, a young clerk, warns the detective with an unsigned note (a spy may be in the office). PART 3 (2026-11-09): the guard has no office key; the final refutes Mr. Nam's three claims and the copy is found in his coat.

Kim Gu is real; his words are made up (dossier fiction). The spy Nam Giho, the list, the clerks, the candle and the police report are made up. The case ends on history: the Provisional Government founded in Shanghai in April 1919 and Kim Gu's police (h1-h3).
